title: On‑Prem CP Bootstrap & Rotation — Ops Sprint Log
body:
Purpose and scope:
This sprint-log style runbook captures the pragmatic steps we used to bootstrap a new private control plane (on‑prem/VPC) cluster, walk through key Terraform module notes, and document the KMS/credential rotation and minor upgrade plan we executed in staging. Intended for SREs and infra engineers preparing a customer or internal on‑prem rollout.

High‑level goals for this run: 
- Fast, repeatable bootstrap with idempotent TF modules.
- Clear rotation and upgrade path with measurable verification points.
- Minimal customer-facing downtime; prefer graceful degraded mode.

Assumptions and target topology:
- 3 control plane nodes (k8s controlplane VMs) behind internal LB, 3 worker hosts for inference.
- Private VPC with dedicated CIDR, peered with customer network where required.
- External facing components limited to a single egress NAT and LB; KMS/HSM accessed via dedicated secure network path.
- Using our terraform modules v0.9.x (see notes) and Helm charts pinned to chart-v1.4.

Quick checklist — prebootstrap (sprint day 0):
- [ ] Confirm CIDR allocations, subnets, and route tables with customer network lead (ticket PD-8421).
- [ ] Get KMS access token + policies provisioned; record KMS key ARN and rotation window.
- [ ] Acquire admin SSH keypair; upload pubkey into vault for TF-managed machine user.
- [ ] Confirm on‑prem firewall rules allow controlplane<->workers on ports 7000–7010 and 9090 for metrics.
- [ ] Create a branch in private-controlplane-terraform repo for this rollout.

Bootstrap steps (idempotent sequence):
1) Environment prep: export TF workspace, set backend to customer S3/minio bucket. Example: 
   export TF_VAR_env=customer-acme; terraform workspace select staging || terraform workspace new staging
2) Validate modules: run terraform init && terraform validate. Flag any provider mismatches (aws provider pinned: 5.3.0 in modules).
3) Plan with limited targets: terraform plan -target=module.network -target=module.kms -out=plan-net.tfplan
4) Apply network and KMS first: terraform apply plan-net.tfplan. Verify subnets, dhcp options, and KMS key ready.
5) Provision controlplane VMs via module.compute. Wait for cloud-init scripts to complete on each node (check /var/log/cloud-init-output.log).
6) Install k8s components using our helm bootstrap job (chart pinned): helm upgrade --install controlplane ./charts/controlplane --namespace redwood --values values-bootstrap.yaml
7) Confirm etcd quorum: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=etcd; ensure all members Ready.
8) Apply CRDs and Redwood controlplane manifests.
9) Smoke test: hit /healthz endpoints of API servers via LB internal IP; expect 200 within 2s.

Terraform module notes (gotchas observed in this sprint):
- module.network: avoid changing public_subnet_count after initial apply — creates replacement resources that require manual route cleanup.
- module.kms: rotation_enabled must be true before key_policy updates are applied. If toggled after the fact, TF will try to schedule a key_recreation; instead do a policy patch using aws-cli.
- module.compute: userdata scripts must use /bin/bash -e to fail fast; we added a small wrapper to write a ready-file to /opt/redwood/instance-ready.
- state locking: customer minio backend does not support lease TTL > 60s; adjust our lock timeout or run terraform in CI with more aggressive retries.

KMS & secret rotation playbook (live rotation executed with zero downtime goal):
1) Prepare: create a new KMS key (alias redwood-cp-rot-YYYYMMDD) in customer account using module.kms_key_create (tf) but do NOT attach policies.
2) Stage: update secrets in Vault to include a second key id and ensure Redwood controlplane supports key fallback in config (redwood.server.kms.primary and secondary).
3) Deploy config change as a canary to 1 controlplane node: patch Deployment with new env pointing to secondary key id and restart only 1 pod. Verify operations continue and logs show KMS calls to new key.
4) Promote: once 1 node stable for 10 minutes, ramp to 50% nodes, then 100% across controlplane.
5) Revoke old key after 48h stable.
Notes: do not destroy old key until all cached tokens and long‑lived services rotate. We observed a stuck exporter process that needed to be restarted to pick up new key.

Upgrade plan — minor (chart patch, zero‑reboot expected):
- Target: Helm chart v1.4.1 -> v1.4.3 (non‑breaking).
- Strategy: canary by label: rollout to namespace redwood-canary (1 replica); if pass health probes for 15min, rollout via Helm rolling upgrade with maxUnavailable=1.
- Prechecks: image digests pinned, admission webhooks healthy, DB migration flag false.
- Rollback: helm rollback controlplane <previous_release>. If helm rollback fails, redeploy backup manifest stored in S3 (key: backups/<env>/controlplane-manifest-<ts>.yaml).

Scaling notes (controlplane and inference nodes):
- Autoscaling disabled for first 72h post‑bootstrap. Manual scale steps: terraform apply -var='controlplane_count=5' to expand compute pool; afterwards run post-scale hooks: /usr/local/bin/redwood-attach-node --verify.
- For inference workers, prefer incremental additions of 2 nodes. We observed degraded batching performance when adding >4 workers at once due to KV cache reshard imbalance. After scale, run cache warmup job: cronjob redwood-cache-warmup run-now.

Verification checklist (post Apply):
- [ ] All k8s controlplane pods Ready.
- [ ] API latency median < 50ms internal, 99th < 800ms for test prompt suite.
- [ ] Billing telemetry shows expected token rates (sanity check with sample generation of 1000 prompts).
- [ ] Logs show no KMS errors and no unauthorized access.
- [ ] Prometheus metrics series for kv_cache_hit_ratio > 0.65 after warmup.

Troubleshooting notes & past incidents captured during sprint:
- Symptom: controlplane node stuck initializing (cloud-init timeout). Root cause: our init script attempted to fetch container image from private registry using ephemeral creds; registry TTL expired. Fix: ensure registry creds are refreshed via vault-agent with longer lease during bootstrap.
- Symptom: terraform plan tried to replace NAT gateway due to lifecycle rule mismatch. Workaround: add lifecycle ignore_changes for tags on module.network.nat_gateway resources.
- Symptom: metrics exporter failing after KMS rotation. Fix: restart exporter pod; long‑lived tokens cached in process prevented rotation.

Open questions / actions for next sprint:
- Add automated terraform preflight tool that simulates destroy/create churn for changed variables (to detect unexpected replacements).
- Improve our module.kms to support staged rotation (primary/secondary) natively instead of manual two‑phase.
- Add a short-lived test harness that runs a focused prompt workload during every upgrade to quantify quality regressions.

Appendix — useful commands and links:
- TF debug plan for network: terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -target=module.network -out tfplan-network
- Check instance-ready on nodes: for node in $(kubectl get pods -n redwood -l role=controlplane -o name); do kubectl exec -n redwood $node -- test -f /opt/redwood/instance-ready || echo "not ready: $node"; done
- Rolling restart single controlplane: kubectl rollout restart deploy/controlplane -n redwood --field-selector metadata.name=controlplane-0
- Confluence design doc: CONFLUENCE:CP-ONPREM-ARCH-2025
- Jira epic: PD-8421

Sprint log entries (short):
- 2025-11-13: Network modules applied; discovered tag drift issue on NAT; added ignore_changes.
- 2025-11-15: Controlplane VMs provisioned; 1 node failed cloud-init due to registry creds TTL. Fixed by vault lease bump.
- 2026-02-27: KMS rotation exercise performed in staging; observed exporter restart requirement.
- 2026-03-05: Helm patch rollout v1.4.2 -> v1.4.3 in staging, canary passed.

Contact & handoff:
- Primary oncall: Ethan Patel (sla pager).
- Escalation: Liam O'Connor (infra lead).
- Doc owner for updates: Maya Chen.

Note: this doc is a working sprint log and not canonical. After this cycle we should migrate stable procedures to the private-controlplane-deploy-onboarding-and-ops-cheatsheet canonical runbook and link out incremental improvements.
